author: United States Department of State
title: Peace and War: United States Foreign Policy, 1931–1941
publisher: United States Government Printing Office, Washington
notes: The State Department's own documentary record of the road to the Pacific war, printed in 1943 while it was being fought, and therefore a collection assembled by one of the parties to make a case. Filed as primary because that is its form — it prints the documents, in full, with their file numbers — and the case it makes is made by selection rather than by alteration. It is where the texts this pack quotes come from: the American outline of 26 November 1941 (doc. 257), Roosevelt's message to the Emperor (doc. 264), the memorandum of the conversation of 7 December with the Japanese memorandum printed inside it and the clock times of the appointment (doc. 265), and the address to Congress and the joint resolution of 8 December (docs. 267–268). Read it knowing what a 1943 collection is for, and beside a work that reads the Japanese side of the same negotiation — source:hotta-2013 is the counterpart in this registry.
